title: Y2K
description:
Where my aesthetic research began back in 2014, with this Imgur album https://imgur.com/a/NGU9j 

It culminated in the Y2K Aesthetic Institute Tumblr, then Twitter, then the full scope of CARI, which I've been co-running with a few others since 2018. 
http://y2kaestheticinstitute.tumblr.com/ 

The term 'Y2K' has become a bit mixed-up over the past few years -- some other terms used online referring to this style are: Y2K Futurism, Cybercore, Cyber Futurism, Cyber Y2K, Y3K, Acubi (sometimes). Additionally, many examples labeled as 'Y2K' actually fall under other styles, like McBling, UrBling, Millennium Disco, Curly Girly, Teenpunk. Note - I think ‘cyber futurism’ might actually be the best term for this style, given that it was used constantly during the time period, along with ‘tech, techno, rave’

title: cyber-femme Being
description:
Nearly 100 years ago, through a silent film in 1927, an image was shared of The Maschinenmensch (literally translated machine-human): an entity known as Futurura/Maria who popularized the robotic woman as a metallic automaton, shaped through body plaster to represent the main character’s former lover.  She was about 5’9, with silver, ethereal armor shaping her tiny waist, her big head, her pointed boobs. As the decades churned on, this girl-bot did not change form in the slightest. She remained in an unnatural and nearly immobile state, an accidental archetype. 

Today, we need her essence more than ever. The things that she purposefully represented: femininity, a future race, a gentle Being that may guide us through technological waves of change. As well as that which she has not yet fully evoked: those of all colors and forms, those with fluctuating weights and gazes, those who hear The Man but may not always relate to Him.

title: Sugar Babies and Black Diamonds: Maroonage Age Daydreams in the Gulf South
description:
Sugar Babies and Black Diamonds: Maroonage Age Daydreams in the Gulf South'' is an captivating exploration of contemporary Black Trans Southern aesthetics amidst an ongoing sense of malaise, backlash and ongoing resistance to the yet-to-fall Plantationocene. It offers a reflective examination of creative endeavors that seek to recreate the maroon space, both during a historic moment of heightened visibility and in the search for communal belonging.
Through a combination of a long-form essay, and photographic images of found plants, family, landscapes. I document my road trip, as I embark on a journey back to my father's birthplace in Waco, Texas. Along the way, I trace the narratives of my ancestors, who forcibly toiled the land and crops, becoming stewards from Houston to Louisiana, immersing in spaces and crevices beyond capture and legibility. An essay that resembles something like a hot summer evening on a screened in porch. I listen closely to what the crickets, cicadas, and plants have to say. I create  a "call and response"  essay and imagery  that encapsulates the sonics of Black Southern Life and Culture in the South.
